This comprehensive guide covers inspectable core memory, archival vector retrieval, multi-agent shared state, custom tools, and portable workflows. The post Stateful Agentic Engineering Copilots with Letta: Core Memory, Shared State, Semantic Retrieval, Custom Tools, Streaming, and Portable Agent Workflows appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> In this tutorial, we build a stateful engineering copilot with Letta that demonstrates how agentic memory extends beyond conventional prompt-based conversations. We begin by creating inspectable core memory blocks that the agent can autonomously update, then expose those blocks for programmatic state synchronization and shared access across multiple agents. We further extend the architecture with archival vector memory for semantic retrieval, a custom server-side tool for deterministic risk estimation, streaming for observing agent execution, server-side message history for persistent conversations, and .af export for portability. Together, these components demonstrate a practical memory architecture in which persistent state, retrieval, tools, multi-agent collaboration, and execution traces work as an integrated agentic system.
